scope: Selected published observations and attributed interpretations, not newly measured genetic data.

observations.locus: PDF p.2, article p.1, introduction and dataset strategy
observations.source_observation: The northernmost South Asian time transect begins around 1200 BCE; the study models an IVC-related profile using individuals at sites in cultural contact with the IVC.
observations.inference_limit: A modeled ancestral population is not an excavated teaching institution or the language of an inscription.

observations.locus: PDF p.9, article p.8, Fig.3B and caption
observations.source_observation: The caption treats ancestry arrows as plausible directions rather than resolved exact routes; the figure labels the South Asian entry path uncertain.
observations.inference_limit: The diagram does not identify the path of a particular technique or text.

observations.locus: PDF p.12, article p.11, admixture dating and modern-group comparison
observations.source_observation: The authors estimate a post-IVC admixture interval and explicitly qualify the contemporary priestly-group comparison for shared ancestry, nonblinded group selection and changing classification.
observations.inference_limit: Present classifications are not direct Bronze Age office records; this study performs no genetic recalculation.

observations.locus: PDF p.13, article p.12, Dravidian discussion
observations.source_observation: The authors present an IVC-associated and a southern/eastern scenario for proto-Dravidian spread, combining genetic, archaeological and linguistic premises.
observations.inference_limit: Neither scenario authenticates a Harappan language or specifies which practical knowledge crossed a contact.
